summary.intent: Autonomously run the full post-execute-phase 'ship' loop for GSD phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust integration + grant-root awareness): verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship as a PR, resolve reviews, and extract learnings — without babysitting, deferring risky/out-of-scope findings to todos.
summary.outcome: Verification, security audit, validation, and simplification all passed; CodeRabbit/Greptile findings were triaged via adversarial verification, yielding 10 applied fixes (incl. a critical read-after-write EIO bug) and 3 deferred todos; PR #594 was opened and reached all-green CI (including cargo-windows after the user pushed the missing 69-14 Windows work) with all 9 review threads resolved; the user-added Desktop E2E hard gate then caught a real, pre-existing cross-client decryption bug (file_iv hex/base64 mismatch between the Rust mount and TS reference), which a debugging subagent root-caused and fixed, with the fix committed but the confirming CI re-run still pending at session end.

repo: cipher-box squash-merges PRs, so branch commit message format never reaches release-please post-merge — only the PR title needs to be conventional/paren-free

pr-release-preview.js's commit regex captures description as `.+` (tolerates parens) and skips merge commits (2+ parents) — the 'feat NN-NN:' reword step is only needed if commits literally use that space-separated non-conventional format
clippy is not gated in CI for this repo; warnings alone don't justify 'simplify' changes
markdownlint excludes `.planning/` in CI, so lint nits on planning docs are non-blocking
desktop-e2e.yml's workflow_dispatch takes no inputs — `gh workflow run "Desktop E2E Tests" --ref <branch>` runs the full macOS/Windows/Linux matrix directly

CodeRabbit CLI times out summarizing full diffs beyond ~125 files/24k lines; `--dir <path>` scoping to specific crates avoids the timeout, but scoped runs hit free-tier rate limits after a few in a row
github-actions[bot] pushes a `chore(release)` commit to the PR branch after checks pass — always fetch+rebase before the next push or it's rejected
git/SSH commit signing can hang and report a false 'commit_failed' even though the commit lands — verify with `git log --oneline -1` instead of retrying
GraphQL PR review-thread mutations (reply/resolve) are occasionally flaky and fail silently — wrap in retry loops and re-query to confirm state
`$status` is a read-only variable in zsh — using it as a variable name in background poll scripts causes silent failures

code.finding: `is_unresolved` duplicated the enclosing `cid.is_empty()` predicate, making it always true and the `pending_content` fallback below unreachable — causing read-after-write to return EIO on freshly-written files (CRITICAL bug caught by adversarial CodeRabbit-finding verification).

`file_iv` was hex-encoded on the Rust FUSE mount while the TS/web reference (`packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts`) encodes/decodes it as base64 — a cross-language contract mismatch that made every cross-client content read fail with 'Decryption failed', undetected by 476 unit tests since the mount decoded its own writes consistently.
`InodeKind`'s derived `Debug` leaked key material via `Zeroizing`'s forwarding Debug impl; replaced with a manual redacting `Debug` implementation.

Own-resolve generation gate intentionally compares the stored floor against itself (not the fetched node's `published.generation`) — a deliberate faithful port of the TS twin's design, not a bypass; external forgery is still caught via the IPNS-signed (seq, CID) binding.
Documented `file_iv` as hex, which was stale and led the Rust mount implementation astray from the actual base64 wire contract used by the TS/web side.

workflow: For security/crypto-critical review findings, spawn multiple independent adversarial-verification agents (each given the 'faithful TS port' and known incident context) before applying fixes — this both caught a real CRITICAL bug and correctly refuted several plausible-but-false CodeRabbit/Greptile claims, avoiding risky changes to live revocation/desync-sensitive paths.
Run heavy resource-intensive suites (full cargo test workspace) centrally from the orchestrator rather than farming them out to parallel subagents, to avoid RAM contention.

GSD's conversational verify-work/UAT skill is unsuited to autonomous, CI-gated phases — for those, bypass it and produce the canonical goal-backward VERIFICATION.md directly via a dedicated verifier agent plus real test evidence.

Dispatch-gated CI suites (like desktop-e2e, which only runs on manual dispatch or specific triggers) can silently hide real cross-client integration bugs for many phases until someone explicitly gates on them — matches the phase-51 pattern of unit tests mocking the boundary and missing the regression.

When static code analysis is exhausted on a subtle cross-language bug, delegate to a dedicated debug agent that reproduces the failure locally with granular logging rather than guessing further from source alone.

friction: The security-auditor subagent stalled mid-stream after ~7.5 minutes ('API Error: Response stalled mid-stream') without writing any output, requiring the orchestrator to manually reconstruct and write 69-SECURITY.md from the already-gathered threat register instead of re-spawning it.
CodeRabbit CLI full-diff review timed out on the 125-file/24k-line phase diff; had to fall back to `--dir`-scoped reviews per crate.
CodeRabbit free-tier rate limiting blocked the `apps/desktop` scoped review for ~46 minutes, requiring reliance on the later PR-level review instead.
A background poll script failed because `$status` is a reserved/read-only variable name in zsh.

`gh` commit and push operations intermittently hung or appeared to fail (SSH signing hang) even though the underlying git operation succeeded, requiring manual verification via `git log` before concluding failure.
GraphQL review-thread reply/resolve mutations failed silently on first attempts and needed debugging with visible error output plus a retry loop.
Parsing `gh` check-run status with space-based field splitting broke on tab-delimited output, requiring a second corrected poll.

The Desktop E2E hard gate (added mid-session at user's request) surfaced a genuine, previously-undetected cross-client decryption bug, requiring a ~23-minute deep debugging subagent session to root-cause — this was necessary work, not really 'friction', but it substantially extended the ship timeline beyond the original plan.
